rationale: One physical arrow press produced two script keydown events on macOS, which made a dropdown advance two entries per press and so appear to select every other item, and made some entries unreachable entirely. AppKit offers every key down to performKeyEquivalent: across the content-view subtree before sending keyDown: to the first responder. Only a Command chord is exclusive to that first offer; a plain key always arrives again through keyDown:, so a host that dispatched from both paths delivered the key twice. The fix keeps the performKeyEquivalent: path for Command chords and lets plain keys fall through to the single keyDown: delivery, and the bridge-side fan-out now skips a bridge that was already offered the key rather than relying on the host to have offered it once. Touching render-assets-and-backends is core/view only: the AppKit host's key-offer gate and the bridge's fan-out guard. No renderer, backend, font, asset or Skia pin changes, no harness or fixture changes, and no public API change. Both halves are covered by confirm-failure runs that break the gate and the skip independently and observe the duplicate delivery return before restoring. Registered as watch-only so the family's coverage stays honest about a change that crossed its selector. No authority moves and no Vellum artifact changes.
